text:
maya: heads-up — gpu provisioning in eu-west-2 is failing intermittently, pods stuck in ContainerCreating with long attach/wait times :grimacing:
ops-bot: ALERT: scratch_iops_high (eu-west-2) — 95th percentile IOps 48.2k — https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/3782 :rotating_light:
sam: details? which nodes, any recent deploys or maintenance windows?@oncall?
maya: looks concentrated on a subset of fleet (gnode-4xx). dmesg shows repeated write timeouts and requeueing. attaching quick iostat snapshot:
```
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         1200  13000  1024000 20480000   1600.0   8.71  18.9   0.5   19.4  0.12  98.9
```
jon: that %util is brutal. did we kick off any background cleaner/GC cycles last night? I remember a config change to reduce retention on scratch images.
meera: we did push storage-cleaner v2.3 at ~2147700000 — it's supposed to be IO-friendly but looks like it's running full-scan on some hosts. also there was a vendor firmware update two nights ago in eu-west-2 (controller fw 1.5.4 -> 1.5.6).
sam: can you grep cleaner logs for heavy windows? try `journalctl -u storage-cleaner | grep "scan start"`
maya: found bursts aligned with cleaner windows, sample log:
```
Mar 07 03:12:01 storage-cleaner[1023]: starting full scan /scratch (throttle=auto)
Mar 07 03:12:02 storage-cleaner[1023]: deleting 1223 temp files
Mar 07 03:12:12 kernel: nvme0n1: I/O 12345 queued for 12000ms, aborting
```
ryan: immediate mitigation: throttle or disable cleaner on affected hostpool, and drain a few nodes to recover GPU capacity. suggestion:
```
kubectl cordon gnode-416
kubectl drain gnode-416 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
systemctl stop storage-cleaner
```
maya: doing that now on 3 hosts in the pool. also raising disk_monitor alert to WARN for the fleet so we can preemptively avoid fills.
sam: +1 on stopping cleaner. also reduce its concurrency: set `SCANNER_PARALLELISM=1` and `IO_LIMIT=20MB` in the unit file, then restart for a controlled restart.
meera: long-term: vendor fw bump might have changed controller scheduling behavior under concurrent GC. we should open a ticket with vendor and roll back fw in the image builds for new hosts until we validate.
jon: ops note — provisioning backlog is causing preemptible/burst nodes to spin up in other regions; costs might spike. estimate current queued GPUs ~36, cost delta ~+$1.2k/day if not fixed within 12h.
ryan: plan: (1) throttle cleaner + drain affected hosts (done), (2) replace 6 worst drives via replacement job, (3) vendor ticket for fw, (4) change cleaner schedule to off-peak 03:00-04:30 and add per-drive IO cap. I'll open PR for the scheduler change.
maya: after stopping cleaner, attach times dropped and 6 GPUs came back online within 8m. logging continued to show some devices with bad sectors, marking for replacement.
sam: follow-up actions: add a repair-label to nodes with >5 write timeouts in last 24h, add a wear-leveling metric to fleet dashboard, and default cleaner to `io_limit` mode instead of `full-scan` for next release.
meera: vendor ticket opened (VT-2248) with logs attached and CFG for reproducer.
ryan: thanks — nice catch maya. please add a short postmortem in /incidents once we confirm replacements so we can iterate on cleaner heuristics. :thumbsup:
maya: will do. thanks all.
